India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the World Happiness Report as of August 2026 is _____.

Finland topped the list for a record ninth year; Afghanistan (147th) ranked last.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Corruption Perceptions Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 91st out of 182 countries in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2025 published by Transparency International, scoring 39/100 (up from 38 in 2024; rank up from 96th). Denmark topped the index with 89; Somalia and South Sudan ranked last (9).

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Ease of Doing Business as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: In the World Bank Ease of Doing Business Index (last edition 2020, since discontinued), India ranked 63rd out of 190 economies. India rose steadily from 142nd (2014) to 63rd (2019/2020) before the index was retired.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Environmental Performance Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 176th out of 180 countries in the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2024, scoring 27.6. Published by Yale & Columbia universities, EPI ranks countries on climate change, environmental health and ecosystem vitality. India slid from 155th (2014) to 176th (2024), weighed down by air quality and climate-policy metrics.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the World Tourism Rankings as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked about 7th in the world by international tourist arrivals in the UN Tourism (UNWTO) 2024-25 data (roughly 18 million arrivals). By tourism receipts India ranked around 9th (about USD 30 billion).

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the World Press Freedom Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 157th out of 180 countries in the RSF (Reporters Without Borders) World Press Freedom Index 2026, released 30 April 2026, dropping six places from 151st in 2025, with a score of 31.96. Norway topped the index; Eritrea ranked last.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Henley Passport Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 81st in the Henley Passport Index (July 2026 edition, published 21 July 2026), with visa-free access to 55 destinations, dropping from 75th in February 2026. The ranking is by Henley & Partners.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Hunger Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 102nd out of 123 countries in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2025, with a score of 25.8 (serious hunger category). Published annually by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Innovation Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 38th out of 139 economies in the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025 published by WIPO, advancing one place from 39th in 2024. India leads Central and Southern Asia and is the top lower-middle-income economy.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Terrorism Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 14th out of 163 countries in the Global Terrorism Index (GTI) 2025, published by the Institute for Economics & Peace (IEP), with a score of 6.411 (unchanged from 2024). Burkina Faso topped the index; only a handful of countries scored worse for terrorism impact.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Gender Gap Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 131st out of 148 economies in the World Economic Forum Global Gender Gap Report 2025, with a parity score of 64.1%, slipping two places from 129th in 2024. Iceland led the index; Pakistan (148th) ranked last.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Retirement Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked last (43rd) among the 44 countries in the Natixis Global Retirement Index (GRI) 2025, which covers OECD members, IMF advanced economies and BRIC countries. Norway, Ireland and Switzerland topped the 2025 edition.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Competitiveness Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 68th out of 141 economies in the World Economic Forum Global Competitiveness Report 2019 (the final edition, as the index has since been discontinued). India scored 61.4 (1-100 scale), ranked 8th among BRICS nations after China (28th). The WEF TRindex was retired after the 2019 edition and replaced by other measures.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Democracy Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 47th out of 167 countries in the EIU Democracy Index 2025 (published by the Economist Intelligence Unit), with a score of 6.96 (a "flawed democracy"), dropping six places from 41st in 2024. Norway topped the index; North Korea ranked last. India was the only major democracy to fall sharply among its peers on civil liberties and the functioning of government.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Human Development Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 130th out of 193 countries in the UNDP Human Development Report 2025 (released in May 2025), with an HDI value of 0.685 (2023 data), placing India in the medium human development category. India rose three places from 133rd in 2022, helped by renewed growth in life expectancy, schooling and per-capita income. Iceland topped the index.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Social Progress Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 109th out of 171 countries in the Social Progress Index 2026 published by the Social Progress Imperative, improving one place from 110th in 2025. India ranks above its income level on Shelter and basic needs but lags on environmental quality, inclusiveness and personal rights. Norway topped the 2026 index.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the IMD World Competitiveness as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 41st out of 69 economies in the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking 2025, slipping two places from 39th in 2024. Switzerland retained the top slot with 100 points, followed by Singapore and Hong Kong. India maintained strong economic performance but was weighed down by infrastructure and government-efficiency weaknesses.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Peace Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 127th out of 163 countries in the Global Peace Index (GPI) 2026 published by the Institute for Economics & Peace (IEP), dropping 12 places from 115th in 2025 amid a less peaceful global trend. Iceland remained the most peaceful country; India is rated a "low" peace category. The 2026 edition was released around June 2026.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Network Readiness Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 45th out of 127 economies in the Network Readiness Index (NRI) 2025, improving four places with a score of 54.43 (up from 53.63 in 2024). The index, published by the Portulans Institute, ranks network readiness in the Applications of ICT. India climbed to 1st globally in annual investment in telecom services, AI publications, ICT exports and e-commerce legislation.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the SDG Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 94th out of 167 countries in the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Index 2026, with a score of 68.3 out of 100, according to the Sustainable Development Report 2026 released by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN). This was India's highest ever rank, up from 99th in 2025 and 112th in 2015. Finland topped the 2026 index.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Slavery Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 55th out of 160 countries in the Global Slavery Index (2025 data, published by the Walk Free / Minderoo Foundation), with an estimated prevalence of 8.0 per 1,000 people, about 11 million people in modern slavery. India sits in the middle of the global ranking; Eritrea and North Korea recorded the highest prevalence.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Travel & Tourism Competitiveness Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: India ranked 39th out of 119 economies in the World Economic Forum Travel & Tourism Development Index (TTDI) 2024 (successor to the Tourism Competitiveness Index), with a score of 4.25, up from 54th in 2021 (adjusted to 38th after WEF revised its methodology). India is the highest-ranked South Asian and lower-middle-income economy; the US topped the index.

India Rankings.subject: Current Affairs
India Rankings.question: India's rank in the Global Financial Centres Index as of August 2026 is _____.
India Rankings.fact: In the Global Financial Centres Index (GFCI 38, September 2025) compiled by Z/Yen and the China Development Institute, India's GIFT City (Gandhinagar) ranked 43rd out of 156 financial centres, up from 46th in GFCI 37, the only Indian centre to feature among the top 15 in the Asia-Pacific. India's other centres ranked: Mumbai 46th and New Delhi 54th. New York and London topped the index.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The Indian Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses: _____ and Rajya Sabha
Parliament & Bills.fact: Under Article 79, the Parliament of India comprises the President, Lok Sabha (House of the People), and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as per the Constitution is _____ members
Parliament & Bills.fact: Article 81 provides for maximum 552 members: 530 from states, 20 from UTs, and 2 nominated Anglo-Indians (before the 104th Amendment).

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as per the Constitution is _____ members
Parliament & Bills.fact: Article 80 provides for 250 Rajya Sabha members: 238 elected from states and UTs, and 12 nominated by the President.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Speaker is elected by Lok Sabha members. The current Speaker is Om Birla. The Speaker is the constitutional head of the Lok Sabha.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Vice President of India serves as the Chairman of Rajya Sabha under Article 64. The current Vice President is Jagdeep Dhankhar.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: A _____ Bill is a bill that exclusively deals with financial matters like taxation, expenditure, and borrowing
Parliament & Bills.fact: Money Bills (Article 110) can only be introduced in Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha can only recommend amendments, not reject them.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: A _____ Bill is a bill that contains provisions related to expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Parliament & Bills.fact: Finance Bill is a Money Bill that deals with taxation proposals. It is introduced along with the Budget.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: A _____ Bill is a bill that seeks to amend the Constitution and requires a special majority
Parliament & Bills.fact: Constitutional amendment bills (Article 368) require a 2/3 majority of members present and voting in both Houses, and in some cases, ratification by at least half the states.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: An _____ Bill is a bill introduced by a private member (not a minister) in Parliament
Parliament & Bills.fact: Private Members Bills have very low success rates. Only 14 have been passed in Indias parliamentary history. The last was in 2016.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: A _____ Bill is a bill introduced by a minister in Parliament
Parliament & Bills.fact: Government Bills constitute the majority of bills passed by Parliament. They are introduced by ministers on behalf of the cabinet.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ is the authorized publication of parliamentary debates and proceedings
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Lok Sabha Secretariat publishes the debates, synopsis, and committee reports. Official records are available on the Lok Sabha website.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Committee examines the financial estimates and suggests economies in government expenditure
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Estimates Committee consists of 30 Lok Sabha members. It examines the budget estimates and suggests improvements in efficiency.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Committee examines the annual accounts of the government and reports on financial irregularities
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members. It examines the CAG reports on government accounts.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Committee examines bills referred to it and submits detailed reports with recommendations
Parliament & Bills.fact: Select Committees are formed for detailed examination of specific bills. Joint Parliamentary Committees (JPC) include members from both Houses.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: Parliament has _____ sessions every year: Budget, Monsoon, and Winter sessions
Parliament & Bills.fact: The three sessions are: Budget Session (Feb-May), Monsoon Session (Jul-Sep), and Winter Session (Nov-Dec). The Budget Session is the longest.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Session is the first session of the year and includes the presentation of the Union Budget
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Budget Session begins with the Presidents Address on the first day. The Union Budget is presented on February 1.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ of the President to address both Houses of Parliament at the start of the Budget Session
Parliament & Bills.fact: Article 87 requires the President to address both Houses at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the start of the Budget Session.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2019 amended the Citizenship Act 1955 to fast-track citizenship for non-Muslim migrants from Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh
Parliament & Bills.fact: CAA 2019 provides citizenship to persecuted minorities (Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Parsi, Buddhist, Christian) from three neighboring countries who arrived in India by 31 Dec 2014.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2020 replaced the Indian Medical Council Act 1956 and established the National Medical Commission
Parliament & Bills.fact: NMC Act 2020 replaced the MCI. It established NMC as the apex regulator of medical education and practice in India.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2020 replaced 9 labor laws and consolidated them into a single code on wages and working conditions
Parliament & Bills.fact: The government consolidated 29 central labor laws into 4 labor codes: Code on Wages, Industrial Relations Code, Social Security Code, and OSH Code.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code 1860 as the criminal code of India
Parliament & Bills.fact: BNS 2023 replaced the IPC 1860. Two other laws replaced CrPC and Evidence Act. These came into effect on 1 July 2024.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Amendment Act 2023 provides for reservation of one-third seats for women in Lok Sabha and state assemblies
Parliament & Bills.fact: The 128th Constitutional Amendment Bill (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) was passed in 2023. It will be implemented after the next delimitation.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2019 abolished the practice of instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) by Muslim men
Parliament & Bills.answer: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage)
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Act declared instant triple talaq void and illegal, making it a cognizable offense punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2019 merged the states of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh as Union Territories
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Act received presidential assent on 9 August 2019, reorganizing the state of J&K into two UTs: J&K and Ladakh.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2017 provides for goods and services tax (GST) — One Nation One Tax
Parliament & Bills.fact: CGST Act 2017 along with IGST Act, SGST Act, and UTGST Act implemented GST from 1 July 2017, subsuming multiple indirect taxes.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2016 provided for the insolvency and bankruptcy code for resolving corporate and individual insolvency
Parliament & Bills.fact: IBC 2016 established a time-bound process (180+90 days) for insolvency resolution. It created the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ Act 2013 provides for corporate social responsibility (CSR) spending by companies above a certain threshold
Parliament & Bills.fact: Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 mandates companies with net worth of Rs 500 crore+ or turnover of Rs 1,000 crore+ to spend 2% of profit on CSR.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ committee is a committee of members of Parliament that examines the action taken by the government on the recommendations of various committees
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Business Advisory Committee of each House determines the time allocation for different items of business.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ is the final authority for interpreting the Constitution in case of dispute over whether a bill is a Money Bill
Parliament & Bills.fact: The Speakers decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final under Article 110(3), binding all other authorities.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: A _____ session refers to the period when both Houses of Parliament sit together for deliberation
Parliament & Bills.fact: Joint sittings are rare. They are called to resolve deadlocks between Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha on a bill. The last joint sitting was on the POTA bill in 2002.

Parliament & Bills.subject: Current Affairs
Parliament & Bills.question: The _____ is the minimum number of members required to be present for the transaction of parliamentary business
Parliament & Bills.fact: The quorum for either House is one-tenth of its total membership (Article 100). Without quorum, the House cannot function.

International Relations.subject: Current Affairs
International Relations.question: With which country did India establish diplomatic relations in 1990?
International Relations.fact:
Key Points:
• India was among the very first countries to establish diplomatic relations with Namibia — on 21 March 1990, the very day Namibia formally attained independence from South Africa.
• India had long championed Namibian freedom, hosting the SWAPO (South West Africa People's Organisation) representative office in New Delhi and supporting independence through the United Nations.

Background & Additional Information:
India was a vocal supporter of decolonization and of the anti-apartheid struggle. It recognized the Namibian independence process through the UN Council for Namibia and refused to deal with the South African administration over the territory. Namibian independence followed UN-supervised elections in November 1989 under UN Security Council Resolution 435.

Post-1990 Developments:
India has assisted Namibia through Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) scholarships, capacity-building programmes and lines of credit. Cooperation spans mining and minerals (diamonds and uranium), agriculture, information technology and defence. Both countries cooperate in the International Solar Alliance and in UN peacekeeping missions.

Geopolitical Context:
The establishment of ties came as apartheid collapsed and the Cold War ended, enabling Namibian independence and rapid international recognition. India's early move reinforced its leadership among the Non-Aligned Movement and the Global South.
Last updated: 2026-08-02

International Relations.subject: Current Affairs
International Relations.question: With which country did India establish diplomatic relations in 1991?
International Relations.fact:
Key Points:
• India established diplomatic relations with Estonia on 2 December 1991, shortly after Estonia restored independence from the Soviet Union.
• India was among the early countries to extend recognition and open formal ties with the Baltic states.

Background & Additional Information:
Estonia declared independence on 20 August 1991 during the dissolution of the Soviet Union. As the USSR disintegrated, India recognized the Baltic republics in line with its support for peaceful change and the sovereignty of the former Soviet republics.

Developments:
India–Estonia relations focus on digital technology, IT, cyber security and e-governance. There is growing cooperation in education and trade in electronics, with regular exchange of business and parliamentary delegations. India's embassy in Stockholm (Sweden) was historically accredited to Estonia before a resident mission was added.

Geopolitical Context:
The normalization took place against the end of the Cold War and Soviet dissolution. The Baltic region has gained strategic importance for connectivity and for the European Union's eastern flank.
Last updated: 2026-08-02

International Relations.subject: Current Affairs
International Relations.question: With which country did India establish diplomatic relations in 1992?
International Relations.fact:
Key Points:
• India established diplomatic relations with Ukraine on 17 January 1992, soon after Ukraine's independence referendum of 1 December 1991.
• Ukraine has historically been a major supplier of defence equipment and components to India.

Background & Additional Information:
Ukraine declared independence on 24 August 1991 and confirmed it in a referendum on 1 December 1991. India recognized Ukraine early and inherited strong institutional linkages built up during the Soviet era, including in defence manufacturing and heavy engineering.

Developments:
Defence cooperation is the bedrock of the relationship — Indian Army T-90 tanks and BMP infantry vehicles use Ukrainian components, and agreements cover repair and overhaul of An-32 transport aircraft and naval engines. Trade, space cooperation (through Antrix), agriculture and pharmaceuticals are other pillars. High-level visits have continued despite the conflict since 2022, with India maintaining balanced ties.

Geopolitical Context:
Relations were established as the USSR dissolved and Ukraine emerged as a key post-Soviet republic. India has pursued defence and energy cooperation while consistently respecting Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Last updated: 2026-08-02

International Relations.fact:
Key Points:
• India established diplomatic relations with Slovakia on 1 January 1993 — the day Czechoslovakia peacefully split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
• Slovakia was recognized by India immediately upon the dissolution of Czechoslovakia.

Background & Additional Information:
Czechoslovakia split into two sovereign states on 1 January 1993, ending the federation established after the First World War. India recognized both successor states on the same day.

Developments:
India–Slovakia cooperation spans heavy engineering, machinery, defence (Slovak howitzers have historically been used by India), pharmaceuticals and trade. There are active educational exchanges and bilateral agreements on investment protection.

Geopolitical Context:
India's ties with both Czech and Slovak republics reflect its recognition of the peaceful dissolution of Czechoslovakia and its continued engagement with Central Europe.

India is a major defence customer of Israel, while Israeli MASHAV and drip-irrigation technologies support Indian agriculture.

Geopolitical Context:
The 1991 Madrid Peace Conference and improving Arab–Israeli relations provided a conducive environment for India to formalize its ties with Israel. India has balanced its relations with Israel while continuing to support the Palestinian cause.

Appointments.subject: Current Affairs
Appointments.question: Who is the current Chief Minister of Haryana?

Saini himself won from Ladwa Assembly constituency of Kurukshetra district, defeating the incumbent Mewa Singh of Indian National Congress, and the BJP formed the government for the third consecutive term.

He was the executive chairman of Mastercard, after having previously been president and chief executive officer (CEO) of the company from July 2010 until December 2020. He retired from this position in December 2021, and joined General Atlantic as its vice chairman.

Appointments.subject: Current Affairs
Appointments.question: Who is the current Prime Minister of India (2026)?
Appointments.fact: The current Prime Minister of India of India is Narendra Modi (as of 2026).  Narendra Damodardas Modi is an Indian politician who has served as the prime minister of India since 26 May 2014. Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat from 2001 to 2014 and is the Member of Parliament (MP) for Varanasi. He is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a right-wing Hindutva paramilitary volunteer organisation. He is India's third-longest-serving prime minister, and the longest-serving prime minister outside the Indian National Congress.

He is a Sunni Islamic scholar, joint secretary of Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama, general secretary of Kerala Muslim Jamaat, a body of various Muslim organizations in Kerala and listed in The Muslim 500.

Appointments.subject: Current Affairs
Appointments.question: Who is the current Speaker of the Lok Sabha (2026)?
Appointments.fact: The current Speaker of the Lok Sabha of India is Om Birla (as of 2026).  Om Birla is an Indian politician from Rajasthan. He is currently serving as the 17th Speaker of the Lok Sabha since first being elected to that office in June 2019. He was re-elected for a second term on 26 June 2024. He serves as a Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha from Kota constituency in Rajasthan since 2014. In 2024, he became the first person in twenty years to be re-elected as an MP to the lower house, after serving as the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and also one of only two MPs to be appointed the speaker twice.

Appointments.question: Who is the current Attorney General of India (2026)?
Appointments.fact: The current Attorney General of India is R. Venkataramani (as of 2026).  R. Venkataramani is an Indian constitutional lawyer and a Senior Advocate in the Supreme Court of India. Appointments.question: Who is the current Governor of Himachal Pradesh (2026)?
Appointments.fact: The current Governor of Himachal Pradesh of India is Kavinder Gupta (as of 2026).  Kavinder Gupta is an Indian politician serving as 23rd Governor of Himachal Pradesh since 2026, He previously served as 3rd Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh from 2025 until his resignation in 2026. Previously, he served as the last Deputy Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir state. Also he formerly served as the speaker of the Jammu & Kashmir Vidhan Sabha.

Appointments.subject: Current Affairs
Appointments.question: Who is the current Governor of Odisha (2026)?
Appointments.fact: The current Governor of Odisha of India is Kambhampati Hari Babu (as of 2026).  Dr. Kambhampati Hari Babu is an Indian politician currently serving as the 28th Governor of Odisha since 2025. He is the first individual from the bifurcated state of Andhra Pradesh and the first Telugu person to serve as the Governor of Mizoram. He served as a Member of Parliament in the 16th Lok Sabha, representing the Visakhapatnam Lok Sabha constituency in Andhra Pradesh. He won the 2014 Indian general election as a candidate of the Bharatiya Janata Party. He previously served as the President of Bharatiya Janata Party for Andhra Pradesh from 2014 to 2018 and first president for bifurcated Andhra Pradesh.

Appointments.question: Who is the current Major Archbishop of Ernakulam-Angamaly (2026)?
Appointments.fact: The current Major Archbishop of Ernakulam-Angamaly of India is Raphael Thattil (as of 2026).  Raphael Thattil is an Indian prelate who serves as the Major Archbishop of the Syro-Malabar Church, the largest Eastern Catholic Church, and as the Metropolitan Archbishop of Ernakulam-Angamaly since January 2024.

Appointments.source: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Appointments.subject: Current Affairs
Appointments.question: Who is the current Minister of Health and Family Welfare (2026)?
Appointments.fact: The current Minister of Health and Family Welfare of India is Jagat Prakash Nadda (as of 2026).  Jagat Prakash Nadda is an Indian lawyer and politician who is serving as the 34th Minister of Health, 25th Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers since 2024 and served as the 10th national president of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) from 2020 to 2026. He is also the member of the Rajya Sabha representing Gujarat since 2024. A key decision maker of the BJP, he is a close aide to Narendra Modi. He was the BJP's national working president from 2019 to 2020. Nadda was also the Minister of Health and Family Welfare in the first Modi ministry from 2014 to 2019 and Parliamentary Board Secretary of Bharatiya Janata Party.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the annual health coverage per family under Ayushman Bharat?
Health & Medicine.fact: Rs. 5 lakh. Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) provides coverage of up to Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: How many families are targeted under Ayushman Bharat?
Health & Medicine.fact: 10.74 crore. It targets 10.74 crore poor and vulnerable families (bottom 40% of the population) identified through SECC 2011 data.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of PM-JAY?
Health & Medicine.fact: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana. PM-JAY is the health assurance component of Ayushman Bharat, launched on 23 September 2018.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of AB-PMJAY?
Health & Medicine.answer: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
Health & Medicine.fact: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana. AB-PMJAY is the world’s largest publicly funded health assurance scheme, with portability across states.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: When was Ayushman Bharat launched?
Health & Medicine.fact: 23 September 2018. Ayushman Bharat was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 23 September 2018 at Ranchi, Jharkhand.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What type of healthcare coverage does Ayushman Bharat provide?
Health & Medicine.fact: Secondary and tertiary care. It covers hospitalisation and follow-up care, including pre- and post-hospitalisation expenses, in public and empanelled private hospitals.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: Is Ayushman Bharat a central or state scheme?
Health & Medicine.fact: Central sector scheme. It is a fully centrally funded scheme, implemented by the states.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of EMI in Ayushman Bharat?
Health & Medicine.fact: Eligible Medical Institution. EMI (Eligible Medical Institution) refers to public hospitals and empanelled private hospitals where treatment under AB-PMJAY is provided.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the life expectancy in India as of 2024?
Health & Medicine.fact: 70.8 years. India’s life expectancy at birth has risen from about 66 years in 2010 to roughly 70.8 years in recent estimates.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is India's infant mortality rate (per 1000 live births)?
Health & Medicine.fact: 30. India’s infant mortality rate (IMR) is 30 deaths per 1,000 live births, down from higher levels a decade ago.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of NFHS?
Health & Medicine.fact: National Family Health Survey. NFHS is a large-scale household survey by MoHFW and IIPS on population, health and nutrition indicators.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of WHO?
Health & Medicine.fact: World Health Organization. The World Health Organization is a UN specialised agency founded in 1948, headquartered in Geneva.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of ICMR?
Health & Medicine.fact: Indian Council of Medical Research. ICMR is India’s apex body for biomedical research, headquartered in New Delhi.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of MMR in health?
Health & Medicine.fact: Maternal Mortality Ratio. Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is maternal deaths per 100,000 live births; India’s MMR fell to 97 per 100,000 in 2018–20.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of IMR in health?
Health & Medicine.fact: Infant Mortality Rate. Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is deaths of infants under one year per 1,000 live births.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of U5MR?
Health & Medicine.fact: Under-5 Mortality Rate. Under-5 Mortality Rate (U5MR) is deaths of children below five years per 1,000 live births.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of PHC in healthcare?
Health & Medicine.fact: Primary Health Centre. A Primary Health Centre is the basic unit of rural healthcare, serving a population of about 30,000.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of CHC in healthcare?
Health & Medicine.fact: Community Health Centre. A Community Health Centre is a 30-bed referral unit providing specialist care for a cluster of PHCs.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of ASHA worker?
Health & Medicine.fact: Accredited Social Health Activist. ASHA is a trained community health worker who acts as the link between the community and the health system.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of ANM in healthcare?
Health & Medicine.fact: Auxiliary Nurse Midwife. ANM is a village-level female health worker providing basic maternal and child health services.

Health & Medicine.subject: Current Affairs
Health & Medicine.question: What is the full form of AYUSH?
Health & Medicine.answer: Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy
Health & Medicine.fact: Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy. AYUSH covers Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy; India has a separate ministry for it.

Education.question: In which year was NEP 2020 approved?
Education.fact: 2020. NEP 2020 was approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 July 2020, replacing the 34-year-old NEP 1986.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the new school structure under NEP 2020?
Education.fact: 5+3+3+4. The 5+3+3+4 structure covers ages 3–18 years: Foundational, Preparatory, Middle and Secondary stages.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of NEP?
Education.fact: National Education Policy. NEP 2020 aims for universal access to schooling, multidisciplinary higher education and a higher gross enrolment ratio.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the new curriculum structure called under NEP?
Education.fact: National Curriculum Framework (NCF). The National Curriculum Framework, developed by NCERT, translates NEP objectives into curricula.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the medium of instruction recommended until Class 5 under NEP?
Education.fact: Mother tongue / local language. NEP recommends instruction in the mother tongue or local language at least till Class 5, preferably till Class 8.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of HEI in NEP?
Education.fact: Higher Education Institution. NEP envisions multidisciplinary Higher Education Institutions with flexible exit options and credit transfer.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of ABC under NEP?
Education.fact: Academic Bank of Credits. The Academic Bank of Credits is a digital storehouse of student credits, allowing transfer across institutions.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of NHEQF in NEP?
Education.fact: National Higher Education Qualifications Framework. NHEQF aligns Indian higher education qualifications with international standards.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of NCrF?
Education.fact: National Credit Framework. NCrF unifies credit systems across school, higher, vocational and skilling education.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of IKS in NEP?
Education.fact: Indian Knowledge Systems. Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) promotes traditional knowledge such as Ayurveda, yoga and ancient sciences in the curriculum.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of SEDG in NEP?
Education.fact: Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups. Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups get special focus for equitable access under NEP 2020.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of NTA?
Education.fact: National Testing Agency. NTA conducts entrance examinations such as JEE-Main, NEET-UG and CUET on behalf of the government.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of RTE?
Education.fact: Right to Education. The Right to Education Act 2009 guarantees free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14.

Education.subject: Current Affairs
Education.question: What is the full form of DIKSHA?
Education.fact: Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing. DIKSHA is NCERT’s digital platform offering e-content and teacher training resources.

First Woman Chief Minister.question: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of India?
First Woman Chief Minister.fact: Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister of India, serving as the CM of Uttar Pradesh from 1963 to 1967. She was also a freedom fighter and a member of the Constituent Assembly.

First Woman Chief Minister.subject: Current Affairs
First Woman Chief Minister.question: Sucheta Kripalani became the first woman CM of which Indian state in 1963?

First Woman Chief Minister.question: Syeda Anwara Taimur was the first woman Chief Minister of which Indian state?
First Woman Chief Minister.fact: Syeda Anwara Taimur served as the Chief Minister of Assam from 1980 to 1981. She was the first woman CM of Assam and the first Muslim woman CM of any Indian state.

First Woman Chief Minister.subject: Current Affairs
First Woman Chief Minister.question: Janaki Ramachandran was the first woman Chief Minister of which Indian state?
First Woman Chief Minister.fact: Janaki Ramachandran served as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu for 24 days in 1988. She was the first woman CM of Tamil Nadu, following the death of her husband M. G. Ramachandran.

First Woman Chief Minister.fact: Rabri Devi served as the Chief Minister of Bihar from 1997 to 1999 and later for two more terms. She was the first woman CM of Bihar and succeeded her husband Lalu Prasad Yadav.

First Woman Chief Minister.question: Sheila Dikshit was the first woman Chief Minister of which Indian state/UT?

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1989?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Sodan Singh v New Delhi Municipal Committee & Another
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Sodan Singh v New Delhi Municipal Committee & Another was a landmark judgment of 1989. Street trading is an age-old vocation and cannot be denied by the government as a matter of right on the pavements and roads of the city of Delhi, claiming that the streets are meant exclusively for passing or repassing and no other use. Only reasonable restrictions could be imposed under Article 19(6). What would constitute a reasonable restriction must be judged objectively on the basis of facts and circumstances in each case. All public streets and roads in India vest in the state, but the state holds them as trustee on behalf of the public.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1989?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Charan Lal Sahu v Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Charan Lal Sahu v Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1989. The constitutional validity of the Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster (Processing of Claims) Act, 1985 , was challenged in this case on the grounds that it deprived the claimant of his right to seek legal remedies against the Union Carbide Company . The court held that as parents partiae, the state was justified in assuming the role of guardian for the victims.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2015?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2015. Struck down restrictions on online speech introduced in Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 .

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2014?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Arnesh Kumar vs State of Bihar or The Arnesh Kumar Guidelines
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Arnesh Kumar vs State of Bihar or The Arnesh Kumar Guidelines was a landmark judgment of 2014. Arrests should be an exception, in cases where the punishment is less than seven years of imprisonment.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1950?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: A. K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: A. K. Gopalan v. State of Madras was a landmark judgment of 1950. Article 21 of the Constitution of India did not require Indian courts to apply the due process of law standard (the specific words used in Article 21 are 'procedure established by law'). Article 19 (fundamental freedoms) and Article 21 (right to life) operate in independent silos; meaning a law could abridge personal liberty of a person as long as the procedure is followed, without any regard to whether the procedure itself is just or fair.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1967?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Golaknath v. State Of Punjab
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Golaknath v. State Of Punjab was a landmark judgment of 1967. Struck down Parliament's power to amend all parts of the Constitution, including Part III related to Fundamental Rights. The judgement left Parliament with no power to curtail Fundamental Rights.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1985?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Olga Tellis Vs. BMC
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Olga Tellis Vs. BMC was a landmark judgment of 1985. The right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution of India includes the right to livelihood.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1992?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Indra Sawhney & Others v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Indra Sawhney & Others v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1992. Upheld that caste was an acceptable indicator of backwardness.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1995?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Sarla Mudgal, & others. v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Sarla Mudgal, & others. v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1995. Principles against the practice of solemnizing second marriage by conversion to Islam, with first marriage not being dissolved. It highlighted the need for a uniform civil code .

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2024?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Association for Democratic Reforms vs Union of India & Ors.
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Association for Democratic Reforms vs Union of India & Ors. was a landmark judgment of 2024. Struck down the Union's 2018 Electoral Bonds scheme. The Court held that the scheme violated the voters’ right to information enshrined in Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution, and that the scheme could lead to Quid pro quo situations.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2024?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Sita Soren v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Sita Soren v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2024. The Member of Parliament and Members of Legislative Assemblies of the States did not have immunity from bribery under the privileges granted legislators under the Constitution.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2013?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Lily Thomas v. Union of India along with Lok Prahari v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Lily Thomas v. Union of India along with Lok Prahari v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2013. MP , MLA /MLC who is convicted of a crime and given a minimum of two years', loses membership of the House with immediate effect.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2018?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2018. Chief Minister, and not the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi , is the executive head of the National Capital Territory (NCT) government.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2006?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Prakash Singh v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Prakash Singh v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2006. Police reforms in India: Fixed tenure of State Police Chief / Director General of Police (DGP) Separation of law and order and crime investigation at the police station level Establishment of Police Complaint Authorities Constitute a State Security Commission; to prevent political interference on the police and evaluation of police performance. Creation of Police Establishment Board Minimum fixed tenure for police officers in operational law and order positions, including Station House Officers , District Superintendents of Police , Commissioners of Police and Zonal Inspectors General. Creation of National Security Commission at the union level.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1997?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Vineet Narain v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Vineet Narain v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1997. Strengthened independence of CBI and Enforcement Directorate ; abolished Single Directive and introduced judicially monitored investigation guidelines.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2013?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh was a landmark judgment of 2013. Held that registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 CrPC if information discloses a cognizable offence; preliminary inquiry only in exceptional cases.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1997?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: D. K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: D. K. Basu v. State of West Bengal was a landmark judgment of 1997. Issued binding guidelines to prevent custodial torture & deaths including arrest memo, information to relatives, medical examination, and production before magistrate.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1994?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Joginder Kumar v. State of Uttar Pradesh
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Joginder Kumar v. State of Uttar Pradesh was a landmark judgment of 1994. Held that police power of arrest is not absolute and reasons for arrest must be justified; protection against arbitrary arrest.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1978?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Nandini Satpathy v. P. L. Dani
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Nandini Satpathy v. P. L. Dani was a landmark judgment of 1978. Expanded protection against self-incrimination during police interrogation; recognised right to silence and right to consult lawyer during questioning.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1980?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Municipal Corporation, Ratlam Ratlam v. Shri Vardhichand & Others
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Municipal Corporation, Ratlam Ratlam v. Shri Vardhichand & Others was a landmark judgment of 1980. The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 empowers the Magistrate to direct the Municipal Corporation to remove public nuisance caused by pollutants.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1996?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: M. C. Mehta v. Union of India & Ors.
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: M. C. Mehta v. Union of India & Ors. was a landmark judgment of 1996. The court ordered creation of Taj Trapezium Zone to protect Taj Mahal from pollution—applying precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle for protection of cultural heritage setting precedent for future rulings on environmental issues.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1996?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: M. C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: M. C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath was a landmark judgment of 1996. Established Public Trust Doctrine in Indian law, holding that natural resources like rivers are held in trust by government for public use and cannot be exploited for private gain.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1972?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Bennett Coleman & Co. v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Bennett Coleman & Co. v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1972. The machinery of import control cannot be utilized by the government to control or curb circulation or growth or freedom of newspapers in India.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1995?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Tata Press Ltd. v. Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Tata Press Ltd. v. Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited was a landmark judgment of 1995. Commercial speech is part of the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression guaranteed by the Constitution.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1978?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: RG Anand v. Deluxe Films
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: RG Anand v. Deluxe Films was a landmark judgment of 1978. Copyright protection does not extend to mere ideas. Where theme is same but presented differently, there can be no question of infringement.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1981?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib was a landmark judgment of 1981. Laid down a test to determine whether an individual, corporation, or society was an instrumentality or agency of the government.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2013?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Swasthya Adhikar Manch v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Swasthya Adhikar Manch v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2013. Laid down the regulations regarding Clinical trials held by Contract research organizations to protect participants.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1950?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras was a landmark judgment of 1950. Ban on dissenting media under the Section 9 (1-A) of the Madras Maintenance of Public Order Act, 1949 struck down as unconstitutional.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1952?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: State of Madras v. VG Row
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: State of Madras v. VG Row was a landmark judgment of 1952. Restrictions on fundamental rights must be just, fair, and reasonable, and arbitrary infringement of rights is subject to judicial review.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1973?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala was a landmark judgment of 1973. Formally outlined and adopted the Basic structure doctrine , limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution by holding that certain fundamental features of the Constitution cannot be altered.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1977?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Stanislaus v. State of Madhya Pradesh
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Stanislaus v. State of Madhya Pradesh was a landmark judgment of 1977. Right to propagate religion does not include the right to convert by force, fraud or allurement.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1979?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Hussainara Khatoon vs Home Secretary, State Of Bihar
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Hussainara Khatoon vs Home Secretary, State Of Bihar was a landmark judgment of 1979. Right to life under Article 21 includes the right to a speedy trial.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1985?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum was a landmark judgment of 1985. Upheld the payment of maintenance and alimony to Shah Bano and hence to Muslim women by Muslim Husbands.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1986?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala was a landmark judgment of 1986. Compelling students to sing the national anthem against their religious beliefs violates Article 25(1) of the Constitution, which grants the freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practice and propagate religion. The freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) also includes the right to remain silent.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2014?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2014. Recognised transgender as ' third gender ' in law and affirmed that the fundamental rights granted under the Constitution of India will be equally applicable to them.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2015?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: ABC v. The State (NCT of Delhi)
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: ABC v. The State (NCT of Delhi) was a landmark judgment of 2015. Unwed woman belonging to the Christian faith can become a legal guardian of her child without the father's consent.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2017?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India or The Right to Privacy verdict
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India or The Right to Privacy verdict was a landmark judgment of 2017. Right to privacy is protected as a fundamental right under Articles 14, 19 and 21 of the Constitution of India thus overruling ADM Jabalpur vs Shivkant Shukla.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2018?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2018. Decriminalisation of acts of Oral sex and Anal sex which effectively decriminalised Homosexual sex.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2019?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Arun Kumar v. Inspector General of Registration
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Arun Kumar v. Inspector General of Registration was a landmark judgment of 2019. The Madras High Court (Madurai Bench) directed the Tamil Nadu state to ban forced sex-selective surgeries on intersex infants ,. the high court of Tamil Nadu , ruled that the term "bride" under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 includes trans women. Specifically, it directed the authorities to register a marriage between a man and a transgender woman.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2022?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Deepika Singh v. Central Administrative Tribunal
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Deepika Singh v. Central Administrative Tribunal was a landmark judgment of 2022. Atypical families and same-sex couples are deserving of equal protection under law and benefits available under social welfare legislation.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2023?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Supriyo v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Supriyo v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2023. The right to marry is a statutory right, not a constitutional right. Therefore, only Parliament can recognize the marriage between non-heterosexual couples.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1978?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1978. A 'procedure' under Article 21 of the Constitution cannot be arbitrary, unfair, oppressive, or unreasonable. A law depriving a person of 'personal liberty' must not violate any of the Articles 14, 19, and 21 of the Constitution.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1997?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Vishakha v. State of Rajasthan
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Vishakha v. State of Rajasthan was a landmark judgment of 1997. Establishment of the Vishakha Guidelines to handle sexual harassments of women at workplace until sufficient legislation is implemented for the purpose.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2006?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Om Prakash v. State of Uttar Pradesh
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Om Prakash v. State of Uttar Pradesh was a landmark judgment of 2006. A person is not convictable under Section 376 2e (Raping a pregnant women) if he had certain knowledge of the fact that the victim is pregnant. The knowledge of the fact must be proven to certainty and not possibility. Consequently, in this case, the accused was sentenced under Section 376 (1), and was sentenced to milder punishment.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1951?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan was a landmark judgment of 1951. Struck down the Communal G.O. of 1927 by the Madras government rejecting caste-based reservations in government jobs and college seats.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1955?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Bengal Immunity Company v. State of Bihar
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Bengal Immunity Company v. State of Bihar was a landmark judgment of 1955. A state cannot tax inter-state sales, unless expressly authorized by the Parliament to do so under Article 286(2) of the Constitution.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1960?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: In Re: Berubari Union and Exchange of Enclaves
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: In Re: Berubari Union and Exchange of Enclaves was a landmark judgment of 1960. Preamble was not part of the Constitution and therefore could not be regarded as a source of any substantive power. However, this view was later reversed in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala , where the Supreme Court held that constitutional interpretation should be undertaken in light of the vision laid down in the Preamble.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1967?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Rajasthan State Electricity Board v. Mohan Lal
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Rajasthan State Electricity Board v. Mohan Lal was a landmark judgment of 1967. The expression 'other authorities' under Article 12 of the Constitution was wide enough to include all authorities of the state; it was not necessary that they perform a governmental or sovereign function.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1975?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain was a landmark judgment of 1975. Examined the validity of the 39th Amendment to the Constitution of India and struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 329A, reinforcing the basic structure doctrine and reaffirming that no one, not even the Prime Minister, is above the law and that the judiciary has the ultimate authority to interpret the Constitution and safeguard its fundamental principles.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1980?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Minerva Mills v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1980. Clarifying the Basic Structure doctrine, the Court ruled that the power of the parliament to amend the constitution is limited by the constitution. Hence the parliament cannot exercise this limited power to grant itself an unlimited power, rendering clauses 4 and 5 of the 42nd Amendment of the Constitution (1976) void.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1992?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka was a landmark judgment of 1992. Established right to education as an integral part of the right to life guaranteed under Article 21.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1994?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: S. R. Bommai v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1994. Court discussed at length provisions of Article 356 of the Constitution of India (President's Rule) and related issues. This helped put an end to the arbitrary impositions seen until then.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2021?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Mohammad Salimullah v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Mohammad Salimullah v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2021. Rejected appeals to provide relief to Illegal Rohingya immigrants from deportation.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2013?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: T. S. R. Subramanian v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: T. S. R. Subramanian v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 2013. Officers of the IAS , other All India Services and other civil servants are not bound to follow oral directives, as they "undermine credibility".

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1991?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: State of Bihar v. P. P. Sharma
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: State of Bihar v. P. P. Sharma was a landmark judgment of 1991. Reaffirmed wide powers of police to investigate; courts should not quash FIR/investigation merely on allegations of mala fides without strong evidence.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1987?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: M. C. Mehta v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: M. C. Mehta v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1987. Introduced absolute liability principle for hazardous industries, replacing English strict liability rule, and established that compensation must correlate with industry's capacity.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 2000?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Church of God (Full Gospel) v. KKR Majestic Colony Welfare Association
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Church of God (Full Gospel) v. KKR Majestic Colony Welfare Association was a landmark judgment of 2000. Approved a ban on loudspeakers or noise in the name of religion, noting that the freedom of religion under Articles 25 and 26, is not absolute, and could be subjected to reasonable restrictions, particularly for the peaceful enjoyment of rights by others.

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs

SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Express Newspapers v Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Express Newspapers v Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1958. Liberty of the press is an essential part of the freedom of speech and expression guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a).

SC Landmark Judgments.subject: Current Affairs
SC Landmark Judgments.question: Which landmark case was decided by the Supreme Court of India in 1962?
SC Landmark Judgments.answer: Sakal Papers Ltd. v. Union of India
SC Landmark Judgments.fact: Sakal Papers Ltd. v. Union of India was a landmark judgment of 1962.
